newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Nov 14.

text.p: General Motors Corp is getting ready to shake up its Delco Electronics unit, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.
- A drug developed by France's Sanofi proved to be safer and more effective than aspirin in preventing blood clots in patients.
- Dominion Resources Inc will buy Britain's East Midlands Electricity Plc for about $2.21 billion.
- Saatchi appointed the chairman of its London office as chief executive officer of its North American operations.
- Dillard Department Stores Inc said its net income fell 38 percent in the latest quarter.
- Microsoft Corp joined with British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp to offer transnational companies private communications networks based on the Internet.
- The United States and the European Union have offered to open their telecommunications markets.
- Three Donnkenny Inc executives sold company shares for $13.4 million between mid-1995 and August 1996.
- The U.S. Federal Reserve decided not to change short-term interest rates.
- Stock fund sales fell 25 percent to about $13 billion last month.
- The NASDAQ Stock Market proposed to set stricter listing standards for companies.
- CSX Corp's decision not to boost its bid for Conrail Inc hints that the gap between its offer and Norfolk Southern Corp's bid does not matter.
- Since Donald Trump's Atlantic City casino Castle was acquired by Trump Hotels & Casino Resort Inc, its stock has fallen and investor interest has waned.
- Profit-taking sent the bond market lower despite the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates stable.
